examples.name: apogee
examples.title: Apogee
examples.description: A three-person design studio for aerospace and climate-tech companies
examples.brief: A design agency site with the confidence of a flight manual: warm off-white paper, a single vivid ultramarine accent, Syne display type at hero scale. The split hero puts a terse studio statement on the left and a thin-stroke SVG orbital diagram on the right, annotated like an engineering drawing. Everything else is quiet — hairline rules, generous margins, numbered lists.
examples.signature: case studies list as numbered flight-log rows, each carrying a small right-aligned altitude figure in the margin

content.theme: a boutique design studio working exclusively with aerospace and climate-tech startups

examples.name: bolide
examples.title: Bolide
examples.description: A demoscene party of size-limited intros, live shader battles, and tracker music
examples.brief: A demoparty site built like a photocopied party invite that fell through a CRT: black-green phosphor background, loud cyan accent, mono type, and deliberately rotated, clipped, overlapping blocks. The homepage collages the party name, dates (3–5 April 2026, a sports hall outside Helsinki), and the compo deadlines into a chaotic-but-gridded zine spread. Scanline textures and chromatic text shadows are allowed; taste comes from committing hard, not from polish.
examples.signature: each compo category is announced in a rotated CRT block with a repeating-gradient scanline overlay and offset red/cyan chromatic text shadows

content.theme: a fictional demoscene party running 4k intro, 256-byte, tracker music, and live shader-coding compos

examples.name: burin
examples.title: Burin
examples.description: An independent type foundry reviving letterforms from engraved bookplates and burin cuts
examples.brief: A one-person type foundry that revives typefaces from engraved sources: bookplates, banknotes, map lettering. A dark specimen-room mood, near-black violet-tinted ground with periwinkle accents and rigorous editorial hierarchy. The first screen splits: foundry name and release list on the left, and on the right a single glyph rendered at viewport height with its counters cut through to the page background.
examples.signature: the hero renders one glyph at viewport height with its counters cut through to the page background

content.theme: revival typefaces drawn from engraved bookplates, banknotes, and map lettering

examples.name: courant
examples.title: The Courant
examples.description: A weekly of sharp notices on experimental and electronic records
examples.brief: A late-night music criticism weekly: near-black ink page, acid chartreuse accent, and a shouting condensed nameplate. Notices run with a genre kicker (MODULAR / POST-CLUB), a dek pulled from the description, and the critic's byline in caps; column rules are thick and unapologetic. The homepage first screen stacks the masthead over a lead notice and a dense ruled well of the week's records.
examples.signature: review scores render as oversized stacked numerals bleeding off the right edge of each notice

content.theme: weekly criticism of experimental and electronic music releases

examples.name: flint
examples.title: Flint
examples.description: Deterministic 2D physics for game engines, one fixed timestep at a time
examples.brief: Docs for a game-engine physics module with an early-arcade flavor kept crisp: off-white ground, crimson accent, Schibsted Grotesk headings, diagrams drawn with stepped pixel corners. The writing is rigorous — determinism, fixed timesteps, collision manifolds — while the chrome winks at 8-bit UI. The homepage first screen shows the module name in a bracketed title bar over an SVG diagram of two bodies at the moment of contact.
examples.signature: headings and diagrams carry pixel-stepped corner brackets echoing early game UI chrome

content.theme: a deterministic 2D physics module with fixed-timestep simulation and rollback-safe state

examples.name: fresco
examples.title: Fresco
examples.description: Civic murals at wall scale, from first sketch to final scaffold day
examples.brief: A muralist who paints civic walls — library gables, underpass piers, harbor silos — and documents each commission from community sketch sessions to the last scaffold day. Loud and joyful: warm white ground, violet accents, Abril Fatface headlines, color everywhere but flat. The first screen is a collage of wall-shaped clipped SVG color fields, each mural excerpted as a flat paint block pinned at a slight rotation, with the artist's name stenciled across the top.
examples.signature: murals appear as wall-shaped clipped SVG paint blocks pinned to the page at slight rotations, like site-plan cutouts

content.theme: civic mural commissions on public walls, documented from sketch to scaffold

examples.name: gouache
examples.title: Gouache
examples.description: Editorial illustration for science desks, from cover art to explanatory spreads
examples.brief: An editorial illustrator working for science magazines: deep-sea features, vaccine explainers, astronomy covers. Cool paper white with a cerulean working accent, wonky Fraunces display, and a masonry wall of assignment cards. The first screen shows the illustrator's name as a hand-set masthead over the top of the masonry grid, each card clipped into an irregular torn-paper SVG shape with a flat duotone fill.
examples.signature: masonry cards are clipped into irregular torn-paper SVG shapes, each filled with a flat two-color duotone

content.theme: editorial illustration assignments for science magazines and explanatory journalism

examples.name: halide
examples.title: Halide
examples.description: A duotone poster series celebrating darkroom chemistry and safelight photography
examples.brief: A poster series shrine to darkroom chemistry: each piece is a duotone SVG poster — developer trays, enlarger silhouettes, fixer molecules — in black plus safelight red. The site is a zine-collage of rotated poster cards, torn-edge clip-paths, and raw uppercase condensed headlines pinned across a chemical-dark ground. The homepage first screen crowds three overlapping posters at slight angles under a huge Bebas Neue masthead, red sprocket strips running through the composition.
examples.signature: every poster carries a punched film-sprocket strip running down its left edge

content.theme: a duotone poster series celebrating darkroom chemistry and safelight photography

examples.name: hallmark
examples.title: Hallmark
examples.description: The CV and selected commissions of an editorial designer for print and screen
examples.brief: An editorial designer's CV that treats the page itself as the portfolio: near-white ground, plum accent, Caslon-flavored display type against a quiet grotesque. The hero splits asymmetrically — name and role on the left, a type-specimen panel on the right. Interior pages fall to a clean single column with hung meta labels.
examples.signature: the hero's right panel is a type specimen of the designer's name set at six descending optical sizes

content.theme: CV of an editorial designer for magazines and book covers

examples.name: hanok
examples.title: Hanok
examples.description: An architecture studio adapting Korean hanok joinery to modern passive houses
examples.brief: An architecture studio site with the warmth of hanji paper and old pine: soft warm-white ground, deep pine-green accent, Fraunces display at generous optical sizes. The split hero sets the studio's philosophy — timber joinery without nails, courtyards that breathe — against a fine-line SVG elevation of a tiled giwa roof. Wide margins, unhurried spacing, small romanized Korean terms as section kickers (madang, daecheong).
examples.signature: section dividers are shallow SVG roofline curves echoing the upswept eaves of giwa tile roofs

content.theme: an architecture studio translating traditional hanok timber joinery into contemporary passive-house design

examples.name: lemma
examples.title: Lemma
examples.description: A notebook of visual mathematics: small proofs and ideas, each drawn as a figure built from compass arcs and straight lines
examples.brief: A quiet notebook of visual mathematics where every idea arrives as a hand-drawn figure. The homepage hero is a compass-and-straightedge construction of a regular pentagon that draws itself stroke by stroke on load, arcs before chords before points, then drifts in pointer parallax as three layers of paper depth. The same point-arc-chord ink notation returns as a construction-line baseline dividing the bands, as a small figure glyph marking each entry in the listing, and as a real inline figure at the head of every proof. Cool white paper, near-black ink, and a single saturated violet for the compass work; Schibsted Grotesk sets the display and Space Mono carries figure numbers and coordinates. The proofs section reads like an engineer's notebook: one construction per entry, drawn and then explained.
examples.signature: a compass-and-straightedge construction that draws itself stroke by stroke on load, in a point-arc-chord ink notation reused as each proof's margin figure, the listing markers, and the section rules

content.theme: visual mathematics explained through hand-drawn compass-and-straightedge figures, one construction per proof

examples.name: lift
examples.title: Lift
examples.description: A bouldering gym in a converted tram depot, open six days a week
examples.brief: A climbing gym with the energy of route-setting tape: warm cream ground, burnt-amber accent, chunky Bricolage Grotesque headlines, rounded hold-shaped blobs as SVG accents. Split hero puts the invitation copy on the left and a stylized SVG wall of colored holds on the right. Buttons are pill-shaped and oversized, like crash-pad handles.
examples.signature: the hero headline climbs a stepped baseline, each word set one step higher like holds on a wall

content.theme: a bouldering gym in a converted tram depot

examples.name: lyrid
examples.title: Lyrid
examples.description: A weekend type-design festival of letterpress, variable fonts, and punchcutting
examples.brief: A type festival that treats letterforms as the only decoration it needs: warm paper white, ink black, one hard crimson. The homepage splits into two asymmetric halves — the left locks the festival name at viewport-filling display scale stacked over the dates (25–26 April 2026, Antwerp), the right runs the workshop lineup as a dense typographic index with heavy rules. No images anywhere; scale contrast and raw borders carry everything.
examples.signature: lineup entries alternate their display-size workshop titles between solid ink and hollow CSS text-stroke outline, row by row

content.theme: a fictional type-design festival with punchcutting demos, variable-font clinics, and a letterpress open studio

examples.name: moire
examples.title: Moiré
examples.description: An interference-pattern library of overlapping line fields and tessellations
examples.brief: An op-art pattern library where every piece is two or three overlapping SVG line fields producing live interference: rotated grids, concentric rings, offset hatching. Near-black green-tinted ground with chartreuse accents makes the white line work vibrate. The homepage first screen pairs a shimmering hero interference field with the top rows of a masonry wall of pattern tiles, each labeled with its line pitch and rotation angle.
examples.signature: two overlapping SVG line fields in the hero drift at slightly different angles to produce a live moiré shimmer, stilled under reduced motion

content.theme: an interference-pattern library of overlapping line fields and tessellations

examples.name: newyork
examples.title: Newyork
examples.description: A weekly newsletter covering New York architecture, hidden infrastructure, and street-level urban design history.
examples.brief: A weekly cultural dispatch celebrating New York’s street-level history and urban design. Set in a broadsheet newspaper aesthetic with column rules, justified text, and heavy black dividers. The bands of the homepage in order are: (1) A masthead band featuring a large SVG typographic 'NEWYORK' logo, the issue number, a date, and a static subscribe form styled as a newspaper classified ad; (2) A main broadsheet story grid band containing a featured lead article on the left with a large typographic headline, and a right-hand sidebar showing a vertical list of previous issues with dates; (3) A footer band containing links to standalone pages, a copyright notice, and a theme toggle. Light mode uses limestone-tinted white with a dark brick-red accent; dark mode shifts to a soot-black background with a desaturated terracotta accent.
examples.signature: the homepage masthead features a stylized SVG typographic wordmark of 'NEWYORK' where the letter 'O' is drawn as a classic circular transit token that spins 360 degrees on hover using a CSS transform

content.theme: New York history, architecture, street layout, hidden infrastructure, and neighborhood design evolution

examples.name: notch
examples.title: Notch
examples.description: Version history for a chiptune tracker with FM synthesis channels
examples.brief: Release notes styled after the chiptune tracker itself: dark plum ground, hot-magenta accent, DM Mono everywhere, faint row-grid textures echoing a pattern editor. The first screen shows the current version inside a tracker-style header grid with channel columns, the latest changes listed beneath in tight mono rows with hex-flavored row numbers.
examples.signature: version numbers render inside a tracker pattern-editor header grid, with release channels laid out as labeled track columns

content.theme: release notes for a chiptune music tracker with FM synthesis channels

examples.name: olivine
examples.title: Olivine
examples.description: Build streaming ETL pipelines with backpressure that just works
examples.brief: Data-pipeline docs with a botanical calm unusual for infrastructure: warm green-tinted neutrals, leaf-green accent, Hanken Grotesk at friendly weights, softly rounded code surfaces. Pipelines are drawn as growing structures rather than boxes and arrows. The homepage first screen shows the tagline beside a curved SVG vine connecting three stage nodes — source, transform, sink.
examples.signature: pipeline stages appear as leaf-shaped SVG nodes joined by a curved vine that runs down the page margin

content.theme: a streaming ETL framework with native backpressure and exactly-once sinks

examples.name: pascal
examples.title: Pascal
examples.description: Risograph and letterpress printing for short runs and stubborn ideas
examples.brief: A print shop landing built like a press sheet before trimming: newsprint-toned ground, harsh black rules, Archivo in heavy weights, and one riso-red accent. Blocks sit slightly rotated and overlapped, zine-collage style, with exposed borders and raw uppercase labels. First screen: the shop name stamped huge, a price-per-run table fragment, and a rotated 'NOW BOOKING SPRING RUNS' slab.
examples.signature: CMYK registration marks and crop ticks frame every major block, as if the page were an untrimmed press sheet

content.theme: a risograph and letterpress print shop for short runs

examples.name: rime
examples.title: Rime
examples.description: Spare dispatches from alpine ascents above the frost line
examples.brief: An alpine climbing log in charcoal blue-black with ultra-condensed Big Shoulders display type and ice-blue accents, stark as a north face. The homepage hero splits: the latest ascent's title and grade on the left, and behind-right, its summit elevation set at enormous scale in ghosted condensed numerals. Interior pages are terse, gear-listed, and unsentimental.
examples.signature: each ascent's summit elevation sits at hero scale in ghosted ultra-condensed numerals behind the post title

content.theme: alpine climbing dispatches from high granite and mixed-ice routes

examples.name: schist
examples.title: Schist
examples.description: Rule catalog and pipeline guides for a multi-language lint runner
examples.brief: Linter docs with a raw, inspection-report attitude: stark white ground, thick black borders, olive-green accent, Archivo set heavy and tight. Rule pages read like citations, with the violating and fixed code shown side by side in bordered blocks. The homepage first screen stacks the tool name in massive caps over a bordered inline search input and the first rows of the rule index.
examples.signature: every rule page leads with a thick-bordered, slightly rotated severity stamp reading ERROR, WARN, or HINT

content.theme: a multi-language lint runner with shareable rule sets and autofix pipelines

examples.name: seoulnight
examples.title: Seoulnight
examples.description: An editor color scheme drawn from Seoul at night: neon signage, river bridges, and late-hour code
examples.brief: The product site for a fictional editor color scheme named for Seoul after dark: a split hero pairs the Latin wordmark with its Hangul counterpart beside a real highlighted code panel, every scheme color debuts as a numbered metro-line roundel, swatches carry Korean landmark names and token glyphs, a full-bleed SVG night skyline with N Seoul Tower drifts in pointer parallax while a lit last train crosses a bridge of eight colored lamps, and a notes devlog records how each hue was tuned.
examples.signature: scheme colors debut as numbered Seoul-metro-style line roundels strung across the hero code panel's title bar

content.theme: a fictional editor color scheme that recolors code in the palette of seoul after dark

examples.name: tabloid
examples.title: Tabloid
examples.description: A loudmouth zine rating small-batch beers and the rooms that pour them
examples.brief: A craft beer zine with tabloid manners: stout-dark page, hot orange accent, huge retro display headlines and cards jostling for attention. Every pour review runs a style kicker (HAZY / CASK ALE), a dek from the description, a byline, and an ABV stamp; the tone is loud but the grid underneath is disciplined. The homepage first screen is the shouting Tabloid nameplate over a packed card grid of the latest pours.
examples.signature: each review card is stamped with a rotated ABV roundel like a bottle-cap sticker

content.theme: irreverent reviews of small-batch craft beers and taprooms

examples.name: torque
examples.title: Torque
examples.description: Low-profile mechanical keyboards machined from single blocks of aluminum
examples.brief: A hardware keyboard maker with a machine-shop aesthetic: raw charcoal ground, signal-orange accent, Big Shoulders condensed capitals stamped like part numbers. Full-bleed bands alternate between spec sheets and manifesto copy, separated by heavy 2px rules. The first screen is the product name over an exploded-view SVG of the keyboard's layer stack, dimension lines and all.
examples.signature: raw spec figures — 45g actuation, 1.2mm travel, 6063 alloy — set at display scale ARE the section headings

content.theme: a keyboard maker CNC-machining low-profile boards from single aluminum billets

examples.name: tuff
examples.title: Tuff
examples.description: A friendly robotics SDK guide for hobby arms and rovers
examples.brief: Warm, approachable docs for a hobby robotics SDK: Bricolage Grotesque headlines with personality, indigo accent, rounded cards, and small robot-arm pictograms drawn as inline SVG. The homepage first screen greets with a big friendly headline, a three-step getting-started strip, and the tutorial tree in the sidebar. Light by default, with a cozy dusk mode and a visible theme toggle.
examples.signature: each tutorial's difficulty renders as a row of one to three tiny robot-arm SVG pictograms beside the title

content.theme: docs for Tuff, a robotics SDK for programming hobby robot arms and rovers over serial and wifi

examples.name: virga
examples.title: Virga
examples.description: Long-form criticism of rain-soaked noir and slow cinema
examples.brief: A film-criticism broadsheet gone nocturnal: dense newspaper structure — masthead, column rules, small-caps kickers — rendered on a charcoal page with a periwinkle accent. Playfair Display headlines carry real editorial weight over justified Source Sans body columns. The homepage's first screen is the front page: masthead with dateline, one lead essay at large scale, and two secondary essays in ruled columns.
examples.signature: each review's star rating renders as a run of typographic ✦ ornaments beside the small-caps kicker

content.theme: long-form criticism of rain-soaked noir and slow cinema
